# Advisories we have assessed and accepted, one GHSA id per line.
#
# A dependency scan that cannot be made to pass is a dependency scan that gets
# switched off. This file is the alternative: an advisory listed here stops
# failing the build, but only after somebody has written down why. Anything NOT
# listed here still fails CI, so a *new* High or Critical advisory is never
# hidden by an old accepted one.
#
# Every entry carries: what it is, why it is accepted, and when it is reviewed
# again. Reviewed at the Saturday team meeting alongside docs/project/risks.md.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# GHSA-2m69-gcr7-jv3q — CVE-2025-6965 (High, CVSS 7.2)
# SQLitePCLRaw.lib.e_sqlite3 <= 2.1.11 bundles SQLite < 3.50.2, in which the
# number of aggregate terms can exceed the number of columns available, leading
# to memory corruption.
#
# Reached transitively: Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Sqlite -> SQLitePCLRaw.
#
# Why accepted, for now:
#   1. There is NO patched version. The advisory lists "Patched versions: None"
#      and 2.1.11 is the latest release, so this cannot be fixed by upgrading.
#   2. Exploiting it requires the ability to submit crafted SQL. This
#      application issues no raw SQL anywhere: every query goes through EF Core
#      and is parameterised, and no user input reaches a query as text.
#      (docs/project/risks.md R11.)
#   3. The database is not network-reachable. It is a local file read only by
#      the application process.
#   4. It disappears entirely if the production store becomes PostgreSQL, which
#      is decided with hosting on 9 September 2026 (ADR-001, AQ2).
#
# Review: 9 September 2026, with the hosting decision — or sooner if a patched
# SQLitePCLRaw is released. Owner: Wenmin Luo.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
GHSA-2m69-gcr7-jv3q
